record.paper_title: Open problems on compact constant mean curvature surfaces with boundary
record.context_brief: star-shaped cmc surfaces with circular boundary
record.original_question: Let Σ be a compact star-shaped surface in ℝ³ with constant mean curvature and boundary equal to a round circle. Is Σ necessarily either the planar disk bounded by the circle or a spherical cap?

evidence.quote: Problem 2.3. Is a compact star-shaped cmc surface of ℝ³ spanning a circle a planar disk or a spherical cap?

artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open problem about compact star-shaped cmc surfaces in ℝ³ spanning a circle. Related results are known under stronger hypotheses (embeddedness plus being contained in a half-space determined by the boundary plane forces a surface of revolution and hence a spherical cap; genus-zero or area bound conditions yield spherical caps). However, no resolution under the sole star-shaped hypothesis was located.

status_evidence.title: Constant mean curvature surfaces with circular boundary in R³
status_evidence.snippet: Embedded cmc surfaces with circular boundary contained in a half-space determined by the boundary plane are spherical caps; general case remains open.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results are available under embeddedness/half-space hypotheses, but the star-shaped case is not settled.

status_evidence.title: Constant Mean Curvature Disks with Circular Boundary
status_evidence.snippet: Genus-zero or area-bounded cmc surfaces with circular boundary are spherical caps.
status_evidence.claim: Characterizations require additional hypotheses beyond star-shapedness.
